Subject: Response from Cascade Legal Rights Project and November 14 clinic update

Cascade Legal Rights Project appreciates the opportunity to respond. We understand why people are concerned. Receiving a letter from a landlord’s law firm soon after asking for help can be frightening, especially when you are already worried about your housing.

Protecting attendee privacy is central to our work. Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Clinic sign-in records are retained internally and kept in locked storage. We do not provide attendee information to landlord law firms.

Magistrate-court eviction filings are public records, and some firms use those filings to send mailings to tenants. Public court filings are a likely explanation for the letters described here. We cannot verify any particular letter without reviewing it, and we will not discuss an individual’s situation or identify clients in this public forum. Anyone with questions about their own situation or our privacy practices can contact us directly.

Our free, walk-in tenant rights clinic is still taking place this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Because the East Atlanta Library meeting room is closed that day, the clinic has moved to the Mt. Zion Fellowship Hall in East Atlanta. The time is unchanged, and no appointment is needed. The accessible side entrance is by the parking lot. People who need help are still welcome, and we encourage anyone with tenant-rights questions to attend.

Questions can be sent to clinic@cascaderights.example. You can also call our office at 404-555-0187. If you have concerns about the clinic or how attendee information is handled, please reach out so we can address them directly while protecting everyone’s privacy.

— Cascade Legal Rights Project
